7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeCertZarChartTrace
8	
9	/-!
10	# Swallow or miss: the shape of an adaptation that can be certified
11	
12	`DivSchemeCertZarChartTrace.lean` shows that the assembler's per-piece no-leak clause
13	*forces* the chart traces `supportLocus ∩ V_b` to be closed.  This file gives the matching
14	sufficient condition, and it is deliberately crude:
15	
16	> if every piece either **swallows** the support (`supportLocus ⊆ pieces j`) or **misses**
17	> it (`Disjoint supportLocus (pieces j)`), then no-leak holds at every piece.
18	
19	For a swallowing piece the trace is the whole support, which is closed by construction
20	(`isClosed_supportLocus`); for a missing piece the trace is empty.  Neither case needs a
21	fibre, a tube, or an idempotent.
22	
23	The crudeness is not a defect, because the necessity lemma pins down exactly how much
24	freedom is left.  Both pinned charts are covered by their pieces, so
25	
26	* if some chart-`b` piece meets the support it must swallow it, whence `supportLocus ⊆ V_b`;
27	* otherwise every chart-`b` piece misses the support, whence `supportLocus ∩ V_b = ∅`.
28	
29	Since `V₀ ⊔ V₁` is the whole relative curve, a nonempty support therefore lies in
30	`V₀ ⊓ V₁` — the divisor must avoid **both** vertical fibres `pi⁻¹(0)` and `pi⁻¹(∞)` — or be
31	confined to one of them.  That is the honest chart-design hypothesis of the lane, and it is
32	where the DD-R atlas has to do its work; it is not something a support tube, a packet
33	idempotent, or a shrink of the base can manufacture.
34	
35	A missing piece contributes nothing at all: its equation is a unit, so its colength module
36	vanishes (`subsingleton_colength_of_disjoint_supportLocus`) and clauses (c1) hold there for
37	free — no fibrewise regularity input.  So the certificate of a swallow-or-miss adaptation is
38	carried entirely by the swallowing pieces, at most one per chart.
39	
40	## Main declarations
41	
42	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.subsingleton_colength_of_disjoint_supportLocus` — a
43	  piece missing the support has a vanishing colength.
44	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.supportLeak_eq_empty_of_subset_or_disjoint` — swallow
45	  or miss gives no-leak at that piece.
46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.forall_noLeak_of_forall_subset_or_disjoint` — the
47	  assembler-shaped `hnoLeak`, with no fibre analysis.
48	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.forall_finite_colength_of_forall_subset_or_disjoint` —
49	  clause (c1)-finite at every piece.
50	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.subset_chart₀_or_disjoint_chart₀` /
51	  `…_chart₁_…` — the design constraint the shape imposes on the divisor.
52	-/
53	
54	set_option autoImplicit false
55	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
56	/- `lake env lean` drops the lakefile's `[leanOptions]` (I-0161); pin in-file. -/
57	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
58	
59	universe u
60	
61	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite
62	
63	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
64	
65	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
66	
67	namespace DivisorAdaptation
68	
69	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
70	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
71	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
72	variable {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
73	variable (A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d)
74	
75	/-! ## A piece missing the support contributes nothing -/
76	
77	/-- **A piece that misses the support has a vanishing colength.** Its equation has a unit
78	germ at every point of the piece (`isUnit_germ_eqn_iff` read through the unit locus), hence
79	is a unit (`RingedSpace.isUnit_of_isUnit_germ`), hence spans the unit ideal.
80	
81	This is the colength companion of `subsingleton_ovlColength_of_disjoint_supportLocus`: on
82	such a piece the certificate's clauses (c1) are free, with no fibrewise regularity input. -/
83	lemma subsingleton_colength_of_disjoint_supportLocus (j : A.index)
84	    (hdisj : ∀ z : relCurve C R, z ∈ A.pieces j → z ∉ d.supportLocus) :
85	    Subsingleton (A.colength j) := by
86	  have hunit : IsUnit (A.eqn j) := by
87	    apply (relCurve C R).toRingedSpace.isUnit_of_isUnit_germ
88	    intro z hz
89	    have hU : z ∈ d.unitLocus := not_not.mp (hdisj z hz)
90	    exact (A.isUnit_germ_eqn_iff j hz).mpr
91	      ((d.mem_unitLocus_iff_isUnit_germ (d.cover.mem_opens z)).mp hU)
92	  exact Ideal.Quotient.subsingleton_iff.mpr
93	    (Ideal.eq_top_of_isUnit_mem _ (Ideal.subset_span rfl) hunit)
94	
95	/-! ## Swallow or miss gives no-leak -/
96	
97	/-- **Swallow or miss gives no-leak at that piece.** If the piece contains the whole support
98	its trace is the support, closed by `isClosed_supportLocus`; if the piece misses the support
99	its trace is empty.  In neither case is a fibre, a tube or an idempotent involved. -/
100	theorem supportLeak_eq_empty_of_subset_or_disjoint (j : A.index)
101	    (h : d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
102	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
103	    d.supportLeak (A.pieces j) = ∅ := by
104	  refine (d.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty (A.pieces j)).mp ?_
105	  rcases h with hsub | hdisj
106	  · rw [Set.inter_eq_left.mpr hsub]
107	    exact d.isClosed_supportLocus
108	  · rw [Set.disjoint_iff_inter_eq_empty.mp hdisj]
109	    exact isClosed_empty
110	
111	/-- **The assembler-shaped `hnoLeak` from swallow-or-miss.** This is the hypothesis of
112	`isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning` /
113	`isCertified_of_noLeak_of_forall_liftQ_injective` /
114	`divisorAdaptation_isCertified_of_noLeak_liftQ_degree`, produced with no fibre analysis. -/
115	theorem forall_noLeak_of_forall_subset_or_disjoint
116	    (h : ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
117	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
118	    ∀ (j : A.index) (s : Spec (.of R)),
119	      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (.of R)).base ⁻¹' {s}
120	          ∩ closure (d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) ⊆
121	        (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)) := by
122	  intro j s x hx
123	  have hleak := A.supportLeak_eq_empty_of_subset_or_disjoint j (h j)
124	  by_contra hxU
125	  exact Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem.mp hleak x ⟨hx.2, hxU⟩
126	
127	section Finite
128	
129	/- The finiteness engine consumes the properness licence on the relative curve
130	(`instIsProperRelCurveHom`), so this clause — and only this clause — needs `IsProper`. -/
131	variable [IsProper C.hom]
132	
133	/-- **Clause (c1)-finite at every piece, from swallow-or-miss.** -/
134	theorem forall_finite_colength_of_forall_subset_or_disjoint
135	    (h : ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
136	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
137	    ∀ j : A.index, Module.Finite R (A.colength j) := fun j =>
138	  A.finite_colength_of_supportLeak_eq_empty j
139	    (A.supportLeak_eq_empty_of_subset_or_disjoint j (h j))
140	
141	end Finite
142	
143	/-! ## What the shape forces on the divisor
144	
145	The necessity direction of `DivSchemeCertZarChartTrace.lean` is sharpened here: because the
146	chart-`b` pieces cover `V_b`, a swallow-or-miss adaptation exists only for a divisor that is
147	either inside a pinned chart or disjoint from it.  Combined with `V₀ ⊔ V₁ = ⊤` this says a
148	nonempty support lies in `V₀ ⊓ V₁`, or is confined to one vertical fibre of `pi`.
149	
150	This is the statement the DD-R atlas owes: **the chart's divisors avoid `pi⁻¹(0)` and
151	`pi⁻¹(∞)`.**  It is a hypothesis about the chart, and it is the only remaining geometric
152	input of the (c1) side of the certificate. -/
153	
154	/-- **Chart-0 dichotomy.** A swallow-or-miss adaptation forces the support either inside the
155	pinned chart `V₀` or disjoint from it. -/
156	theorem subset_chart₀_or_disjoint_chart₀
157	    (h : ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
158	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
159	    d.supportLocus ⊆ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ : Set (relCurve C R))
160	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus
161	        ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ : Set (relCurve C R)) := by
162	  by_cases hmeet : ∃ j : Fin A.m₀, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces (Sum.inl j) : Set (relCurve C R))
163	  · obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := hmeet
164	    exact Or.inl (hj.trans fun x hx => (relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (A.h₀ j) hx)
165	  · refine Or.inr (Set.disjoint_iff_inter_eq_empty.mpr ?_)
166	    rw [A.supportLocus_inter_chart₀_eq_iUnion]
167	    refine Set.iUnion_eq_empty.mpr fun j => Set.disjoint_iff_inter_eq_empty.mp ?_
168	    exact (h (Sum.inl j)).resolve_left fun hsub => hmeet ⟨j, hsub⟩
169	
170	/-- **Chart-1 dichotomy.** -/
171	theorem subset_chart₁_or_disjoint_chart₁
172	    (h : ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
173	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
174	    d.supportLocus ⊆ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : Set (relCurve C R))
175	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus
176	        ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : Set (relCurve C R)) := by
177	  by_cases hmeet : ∃ j : Fin A.m₁, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces (Sum.inr j) : Set (relCurve C R))
178	  · obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := hmeet
179	    exact Or.inl (hj.trans fun x hx => (relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (A.h₁ j) hx)
180	  · refine Or.inr (Set.disjoint_iff_inter_eq_empty.mpr ?_)
181	    rw [A.supportLocus_inter_chart₁_eq_iUnion]
182	    refine Set.iUnion_eq_empty.mpr fun j => Set.disjoint_iff_inter_eq_empty.mp ?_
183	    exact (h (Sum.inr j)).resolve_left fun hsub => hmeet ⟨j, hsub⟩
184	
185	end DivisorAdaptation
186	
187	end AlgebraicGeometry
188

Q1. **Is the lane now converging, or did I just relabel a wall?** Compare the shape of the obligation before (produce `hnoLeak` for `ThetaGeneratorSeed.divisorAdaptation`, which is `(exists_divisorAdaptation ...).some`) and after (arrange that the chart's divisors avoid `pi⁻¹(0)` and `pi⁻¹(∞)`, then construct a swallow-or-miss adaptation). Is the new obligation genuinely more tractable, or is `chart-avoid` just as hard as what it replaced?

Q2. **Is `chart-avoid` even TRUE for the DD-R universal family?** This is the crux. Read `informal/spec-dd-r.md` (especially ADDENDUM 1, which asserts "the universal family of DDR-3/4 is honestly certified over each Z(♦)-chart ring"), the DD-R chart construction (`DivSchemeEpsCarve*.lean`, `Pic0ChartLocusOpen.lean`, `Pic0ChartLocusFibreField.lean`, `DivSchemeAtlasFactor.lean`), and the theta-window setup (`relThetaSections`, `ThetaGeneratorSeed` in `DivSchemeFamily.lean`). If the chart does NOT, then either (a) the atlas must be redesigned to add that condition, or (b) my necessity theorem shows the whole `IsCertified`/`DivFamZar` design cannot classify the divisors it claims to. Which is it? This determines whether the next session builds a lemma or redesigns the functor.

Q3. **Is `DivFamZar` the right functor at all?** If `IsCertified` is unsatisfiable for divisors meeting both vertical fibres in a connected way, then `DivFamZar C R pi n` is a proper subfunctor of the honest relative-divisor functor, and `divRep : (divFunctor g).RepresentableBy (DivScheme g)` would represent the wrong thing. Check whether anything in the project pins `divFunctor` to the honest divisor functor, and whether I-0213's adjudication (DivFam is not a Zariski sheaf) already conceded this ground.

Q4. **Given the recon finding that the certificate lane is one of six independent mountains and that `dat-g` has no spec, no worksheet and no Lean file — is continuing to spend rounds on the certificate the right allocation?** Give me a concrete recommendation for what the NEXT session on this task should do, ranked, with a one-line justification each. Include an honest assessment of whether "close representability of Pic^0" is achievable at all in the current design, or whether the honest move is to tell the human it needs a redesign decision.

Q5. Anything I got wrong, overclaimed, or left broken. Check the roadmap tree for incoherence after my edits and the two Lean files for statements that do not say what their docstrings claim.

You are read-only on source. File inbox `issue`/`memory` items for what you find, and give me a blunt verdict.

Base directory for this skill: /home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/horizon

You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.

## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate

Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.

You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
**shared state**, not meetings:

- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
  another team.
- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).

Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
commands (unread inbox for your task, your session's runtime/tokens, other live
runs) — read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone.

## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)

**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.

The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):

- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.

## Your session's identity (environment variables)

The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |

## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)

Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:

- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).

## One-shot discipline (important)

This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).

## Pick the highest-value work

Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.

If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
the objective is large. Leave a `"$HORIZON_BIN" task comment <task_id> --body …`
at each significant step. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
(it returns to the queue).

## Fresh-context checkpoints

The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
checkpoints:

- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
  clean/build result.

Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
terminal `done` claim.

Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.

## Warnings are work

Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
why.

Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
issue rather than repeated no-op calls.

## Do the work (Lean)

For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
configured final build covers the same files.

**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
mathlib — query it:

| You want | Use | Not |
|---|---|---|
| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |

`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
back to grep.

Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.

- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.

## Read the other projects

They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.

## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)

Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
needs no permission.

Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.

## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)

Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).

Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:

- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
  as **memory**.

Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
shorter. This pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.

## Resuming after an interruption

State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:

- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.

## Final report (your last message)

Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
Recommended sections: `## Summary`, `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
`## Why I stopped`, `## Next` (keep at least `## Progress` and
`## Why I stopped`). In `## Progress`, one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
not by itself a reason to stop.

## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)

There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the
`subagents` skill):

- **janitor** — workspace hygiene: roadmap/READMEs concise, inbox from overflowing.
- **ground** — workspace-wide strategy, graph, ledger, and convergence review.
- **work-reviewer** — fresh-context review of your last work; is it converging?
- **blueprint** — Lean ↔ blueprint statement/`\uses` correctness for a scoped slice.
- **reference-retriever**, **debug**, **page-transcriber** — as needed.

Keep proving; delegate the upkeep.

"""Advisory health checks for the human/agent-maintained work queues.

These checks deliberately never mutate state or fail a command.  They make the
workspace-hygiene guidance executable and visible to every CLI caller while
leaving room for a human or agent to decide that an unusually large collection
is intentional.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

from .clock import utc_now
from .inbox import InboxItem, InboxKind, InboxStatus
from .roadmap import RoadmapItem, RoadmapStatus
from .tasks import HorizonTask, TaskStatus


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class AdvisoryHealthLimits:
    """Central defaults for CLI collection-health warnings."""

    open_memories: int = 10
    open_info: int = 4
    open_inbox: int = 30
    open_tasks: int = 12
    active_roadmap: int = 8
    stale_running_task_hours: int = 24


DEFAULT_HEALTH_LIMITS = AdvisoryHealthLimits()


def _as_utc(value: datetime) -> datetime:
    """Normalize legacy naive timestamps before comparing their age."""
    if value.tzinfo is None:
        return value.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    return value.astimezone(timezone.utc)


def inbox_health_warnings(
    items: Sequence[InboxItem], limits: AdvisoryHealthLimits = DEFAULT_HEALTH_LIMITS
) -> list[str]:
    """Warnings for an inbox whose open working set may need pruning."""
    open_items = [item for item in items if item.status is InboxStatus.OPEN]
    warnings: list[str] = []
    counts = {
        kind: sum(item.kind is kind for item in open_items)
        for kind in (InboxKind.MEMORY, InboxKind.INFO)
    }
    if counts[InboxKind.MEMORY] > limits.open_memories:
        warnings.append(
            f"Inbox has {counts[InboxKind.MEMORY]} open memory items "
            f"(recommended maximum {limits.open_memories}) — archive stale, "
            "superseded, or no-longer-key memories if this is not intentional."
        )
    if counts[InboxKind.INFO] > limits.open_info:
        warnings.append(
            f"Inbox has {counts[InboxKind.INFO]} open info items "
            f"(recommended maximum {limits.open_info}) — archive notices that "
            "have been consumed if this is not intentional."
        )
    working_set = [item for item in open_items if item.kind is not InboxKind.PROTECTION]
    if len(working_set) > limits.open_inbox:
        warnings.append(
            f"Inbox has {len(working_set)} open non-protection items "
            f"(recommended maximum {limits.open_inbox}) — review duplicates and "
            "stale items; use `inbox complete` or `inbox archive` where appropriate."
        )
    return warnings


def task_health_warnings(
    tasks: Sequence[HorizonTask],
    limits: AdvisoryHealthLimits = DEFAULT_HEALTH_LIMITS,
    *,
    now: datetime | None = None,
) -> list[str]:
    """Warnings for an oversized task queue or apparently orphaned runs."""
    open_statuses = {TaskStatus.QUEUED, TaskStatus.RUNNING, TaskStatus.BLOCKED}
    open_tasks = [task for task in tasks if task.status in open_statuses]
    warnings: list[str] = []
    if len(open_tasks) > limits.open_tasks:
        warnings.append(
            f"Task queue has {len(open_tasks)} open tasks "
            f"(recommended maximum {limits.open_tasks}) — review whether some "
            "objectives are done, blocked, cancelled, duplicated, or better kept "
            "only as roadmap milestones."
        )

    cutoff = _as_utc(now or utc_now()) - timedelta(hours=limits.stale_running_task_hours)
    stale = [
        task for task in tasks
        if task.status is TaskStatus.RUNNING and _as_utc(task.updated_at) < cutoff
    ]
    if stale:
        shown = ", ".join(task.id for task in stale[:4])
        more = f" (+{len(stale) - 4} more)" if len(stale) > 4 else ""
        warnings.append(
            f"Task(s) {shown}{more} have remained running for more than "
            f"{limits.stale_running_task_hours}h — confirm a run is still live or "
            "reset their status if it ended unexpectedly."
        )
    return warnings


def roadmap_health_warnings(
    items: Sequence[RoadmapItem], limits: AdvisoryHealthLimits = DEFAULT_HEALTH_LIMITS
) -> list[str]:
    """Warnings when too many roadmap milestones claim simultaneous focus."""
    active = [item for item in items if item.status is RoadmapStatus.ACTIVE]
    if len(active) <= limits.active_roadmap:
        return []
    return [
        f"Roadmap has {len(active)} active items "
        f"(recommended maximum {limits.active_roadmap}) — consider marking "
        "deferred work pending, or leave the broader focus active intentionally."
    ]

208	end FinCoverData

210	/-- Restriction of sections of the relative curve as an `R`-algebra homomorphism
211	(`Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra` structures on both sides). -/
212	noncomputable def relResAlgHom {W V : (relCurve C R).Opens} (h : W ≤ V) :
213	    Γ(relCurve C R, V) →ₐ[R] Γ(relCurve C R, W) :=
214	  AlgHom.mk' (CommRingCat.Hom.hom ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op))
215	    (fun c x => by
216	      simp only [Algebra.smul_def]
217	      rw [map_mul]
218	      congr 1
219	      rw [Scheme.algebraMap_overSectionsAlgebra, Scheme.algebraMap_overSectionsAlgebra]
220	      exact (relCurve C R).overAlgebraMap_apply_res R (homOfLE h).op c)

223	lemma relResAlgHom_apply {W V : (relCurve C R).Opens} (h : W ≤ V) (s : Γ(relCurve C R, V)) :
224	    relResAlgHom C R h s = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op).hom s :=
225	  rfl

227	/-- **The finite chart adaptation of a local-equation system** (worksheet §1.1 (D1)):
228	basic-open cover data of the two pinned charts, equations `f_j` on the pieces, and the
229	pointwise refinement clause `eqn_rel` — on the overlap of each piece with any member of
230	`d.cover`, `f_j` agrees with `d`'s equation up to a unit. Regularity of the `f_j` is
231	DERIVED (`DivisorAdaptation.eqn_regular`), not stored. -/
232	structure DivisorAdaptation [IsAffineHom π] (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) :
233	    Type u extends FinCoverData C R π where
234	  /-- The equation on the piece `D(h_j)`. -/
235	  eqn : ∀ j : toFinCoverData.index, Γ(relCurve C R, toFinCoverData.pieces j)
236	  /-- The equations refine `d` pointwise up to units: on the overlap of each piece with
237	  any member of `d`'s cover, `f_j` and `d`'s equation differ by a unit. Point-free (the
238	  `DivEq` spelling), so it pulls back along arbitrary morphisms — the resolution of the
239	  DD-1 pt-transport seam (`informal/spec-dd-2.md` §1a). The quantifier ranges over ALL
240	  `y`: the empty overlap carries the zero ring, where the clause is trivial. -/
241	  eqn_rel : ∀ (j : toFinCoverData.index) (y : relCurve C R),
242	    ∃ u : Γ(relCurve C R, toFinCoverData.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y)ˣ,
243	      ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom (eqn j)
244	        = (u : Γ(relCurve C R, toFinCoverData.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y))
245	          * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_right).op).hom (d.eqn y)
246	
247	namespace DivisorAdaptation
248	
249	variable {C R π} [IsAffineHom π] {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
250	variable (A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d)
251	
252	/-- **The compatibility constructor from anchored refinement data** (the pre-DD-2 field
253	layout): a base point `pt j` of `d.cover` per piece with `pieces j ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j)`
254	and a comparison unit `eqn j = unit j · res (d.eqn (pt j))`. The pointwise clause
255	`eqn_rel` is derived by rewriting `d.eqn (pt j)` into `d.eqn y` through the transition
256	unit `d.ratioUnit (pt j) y` on the overlap (the `DivEq.trans` calc pattern). -/
257	def ofAnchors (D : FinCoverData C R π)
258	    (eqn : ∀ j : D.index, Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j))
259	    (pt : D.index → relCurve C R)
260	    (piece_le : ∀ j, D.pieces j ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j))
261	    (unit : ∀ j, Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j)ˣ)
262	    (eqn_eq : ∀ j, eqn j = (unit j : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j))
263	      * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (piece_le j)).op).hom (d.eqn (pt j))) :
264	    DivisorAdaptation C R π d where
265	  toFinCoverData := D
266	  eqn := eqn
267	  eqn_rel := fun j y => by
268	    have hWle : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y
269	        ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j) ⊓ d.cover.opens y :=
270	      inf_le_inf (piece_le j) le_rfl
271	    have E1 := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE
272	      (inf_le_left : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j)).op).hom (eqn_eq j)
273	    rw [map_mul, Scheme.LocalEquations.res_res] at E1
274	    have E2 := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE hWle).op).hom
275	      (d.eqn_restrict_eq (pt j) y)
276	    rw [map_mul, Scheme.LocalEquations.res_res, Scheme.LocalEquations.res_res] at E2
277	    refine ⟨(relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)
278	      * (relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y), ?_⟩
279	    rw [Units.val_mul]
280	    calc ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom (eqn j)
281	        = ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)).val
282	          * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE
283	              ((inf_le_left : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j).trans
284	                (piece_le j))).op).hom (d.eqn (pt j)) := by
285	          rw [show ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict (inf_le_left :
286	              D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j) (unit j)).val
287	              = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left :
288	                  D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j)).op).hom (unit j).val
289	            from rfl]
290	          exact E1
291	      _ = ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)).val
292	          * (((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y)).val
293	            * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (hWle.trans
294	                (inf_le_right : d.cover.opens (pt j) ⊓ d.cover.opens y
295	                  ≤ d.cover.opens y))).op).hom (d.eqn y)) := by
296	          rw [show ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y)).val
297	              = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map
298	                  (homOfLE hWle).op).hom (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y).val from rfl]
299	          rw [E2]
300	      _ = ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)).val
301	          * ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y)).val
302	          * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE
303	              (inf_le_right : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y
304	                ≤ d.cover.opens y)).op).hom (d.eqn y) := by
305	          rw [mul_assoc]
306	
307	/-- The adaptation's equations are regular: at `z ∈ D(h_j)` the pointwise clause
308	`eqn_rel j z` presents the germ of `f_j` as a unit germ times the germ of `d`'s regular
309	equation at the member of `z` itself. -/
310	theorem eqn_regular (j : A.index) (z : relCurve C R) (hz : z ∈ A.pieces j) :
311	    ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces j) z hz).hom (A.eqn j)
312	      ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C R).presheaf.stalk z) := by
313	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := A.eqn_rel j z
314	  have hzW : z ∈ A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z := ⟨hz, d.cover.mem_opens z⟩
315	  have hgerm : ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces j) z hz).hom (A.eqn j)
316	      = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom
317	          (u : Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z))
318	        * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens z) z
319	            (d.cover.mem_opens z)).hom (d.eqn z) := by
320	    have h := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ
321	      (A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom hu
322	    rw [map_mul, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply] at h
323	    exact h
324	  rw [hgerm]
325	  exact mul_mem
326	    ((u.isUnit.map ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ
327	      (A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom).mem_nonZeroDivisors)
328	    (d.regular z z (d.cover.mem_opens z))
329	
330	/-! ### The colength modules and the glued equalizer -/
331	
332	/-- The chart-local colength module `Γ(D(h_j)) ⧸ (f_j)`, an `R`-algebra through
333	`Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra`. -/
334	noncomputable abbrev colength (j : A.index) : Type u :=
335	  Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j) ⧸ Ideal.span {A.eqn j}
336	
337	/-- The symmetric overlap ideal: both equations restricted to the piece overlap. The
338	two restrictions generate the same ideal (the equations differ by units on overlaps
339	through the refinement witness), but the symmetric span needs no transport in the
340	DEFINITION. -/
341	noncomputable abbrev ovlIdeal (i j : A.index) :
342	    Ideal Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j) :=
343	  Ideal.span
344	    {relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_left : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces i) (A.eqn i),
345	     relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_right : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces j) (A.eqn j)}
346	
347	/-- The overlap colength module `Γ(D(h_i) ⊓ D(h_j)) ⧸ (f_i, f_j)`. -/
348	noncomputable abbrev ovlColength (i j : A.index) : Type u :=
349	  Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j) ⧸ A.ovlIdeal i j
350	
351	/-- The induced `R`-algebra map `colength i → ovlColength i j` (restrict, then quotient;
352	the ideal of `f_i` lands in the symmetric span). -/
353	noncomputable def toOvlLeft (i j : A.index) : A.colength i →ₐ[R] A.ovlColength i j :=
354	  Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ (Ideal.span {A.eqn i})
355	    ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R (A.ovlIdeal i j)).comp (relResAlgHom C R inf_le_left))
356	    (by
357	      intro a ha
358	      rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at ha
359	      obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := ha
360	      simp only [AlgHom.comp_apply, map_mul]
361	      have hmem : relResAlgHom C R
362	          (inf_le_left : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces i) (A.eqn i)
363	          ∈ A.ovlIdeal i j :=
364	        Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_insert _ _)
365	      rw [Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ_eq_mk, Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr hmem, zero_mul])
366	
367	/-- The induced `R`-algebra map `colength j → ovlColength i j`. -/
368	noncomputable def toOvlRight (i j : A.index) : A.colength j →ₐ[R] A.ovlColength i j :=
369	  Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ (Ideal.span {A.eqn j})
370	    ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R (A.ovlIdeal i j)).comp (relResAlgHom C R inf_le_right))
371	    (by
372	      intro a ha
373	      rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at ha
374	      obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := ha
375	      simp only [AlgHom.comp_apply, map_mul]
376	      have hmem : relResAlgHom C R
377	          (inf_le_right : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces j) (A.eqn j)
378	          ∈ A.ovlIdeal i j :=
379	        Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_insert_of_mem _ rfl)
380	      rw [Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ_eq_mk, Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr hmem, zero_mul])
381	
382	/-- The product of the chart-local colength modules (an `abbrev`, so the `Pi.module`
383	instances apply directly — probe finding, spec §1b(iii)). -/
384	noncomputable abbrev chartProd : Type u := ∀ j : A.index, A.colength j
385	
386	/-- The product of the overlap colength modules over ordered index pairs. -/
387	noncomputable abbrev ovlProd : Type u := ∀ p : A.index × A.index, A.ovlColength p.1 p.2
388	
389	/-- The left arrow of the equalizer: restrict the `p.1` component to each overlap. -/
390	noncomputable def deltaLeft : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
391	  LinearMap.pi
392	    (fun p : A.index × A.index => (A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.1)
393	
394	/-- The right arrow of the equalizer: restrict the `p.2` component to each overlap. -/
395	noncomputable def deltaRight : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
396	  LinearMap.pi
397	    (fun p : A.index × A.index => (A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.2)
398	
399	/-- **The glued colength module `W(d)`** (worksheet §1.1 (c2)): the equalizer of the two
400	overlap-restriction arrows on the product of chart-local colengths, spelled as the
401	kernel of their difference (so the `FlatCokernel` base-change keystone applies
402	verbatim); the equalizer description is `mem_gluedSubmodule_iff`. -/
403	noncomputable def gluedSubmodule : Submodule R A.chartProd :=
404	  LinearMap.ker (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight)
405	
406	/-- The equalizer description of the glued colength module: componentwise agreement of
407	the two overlap restrictions. -/
408	lemma mem_gluedSubmodule_iff (s : A.chartProd) :
409	    s ∈ A.gluedSubmodule ↔ ∀ p : A.index × A.index,
410	      A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2 (s p.1) = A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2 (s p.2) := by
411	  simp only [gluedSubmodule, LinearMap.mem_ker, LinearMap.sub_apply, sub_eq_zero,
412	    funext_iff, deltaLeft, deltaRight, LinearMap.pi_apply, LinearMap.coe_comp,
413	    Function.comp_apply, LinearMap.proj_apply, AlgHom.toLinearMap_apply]
414	
415	/-- The glued colength module, as a type. -/
416	noncomputable abbrev Glued : Type u := ↥A.gluedSubmodule
417	
418	/-! ### The certificate -/
419	
420	/-- **The colength certificate** (worksheet §1.1 (c1)/(c2) in the spec-dd-1 §1c frozen
421	spelling): chart-local colengths finite projective over `R` (c1); the glued module
422	finite projective of constant fibre rank `n` — honest finrank at every prime through
423	`Module.rankAtStalk` (c2); and the two flat-cokernel clauses (c3)/(c4) that make
424	certificates base-change along ARBITRARY test maps (trivial over a field; transported
425	by right-exactness; consumed by `FlatCokernel.tensorKer_bijective_of_flat_coker`). -/
426	structure IsCertified (n : ℕ) : Prop where
427	  /-- (c1) Each chart-local colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
428	  finite_colength : ∀ j, Module.Finite R (A.colength j)
429	  /-- (c1) Each chart-local colength module is projective over `R`. -/
430	  projective_colength : ∀ j, Module.Projective R (A.colength j)
431	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
432	  finite_glued : Module.Finite R A.Glued
433	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is projective over `R`. -/
434	  projective_glued : Module.Projective R A.Glued
435	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module has constant fibre rank `n`. -/
436	  rankAtStalk_glued : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, Module.rankAtStalk A.Glued p = n
437	  /-- (c3) The cokernel of `W(d) ↪ Π_j colength j` is flat. -/
438	  flat_coker_incl : Module.Flat R (A.chartProd ⧸ A.gluedSubmodule)
439	  /-- (c4) The cokernel of the difference arrow is flat. -/
440	  flat_coker_diff :
441	    Module.Flat R (A.ovlProd ⧸ LinearMap.range (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight))
442	
443	end DivisorAdaptation
444	
445	/-! ## The certified family and the divisor-functor value -/
446	
447	variable (n : ℕ)
448	
449	/-- **A certified divisor family of degree `n` over the test ring `R`** (the worksheet's
450	(D1) pair `(d, c)`): a local-equation system with a certified finite chart
451	adaptation. -/
452	structure CertifiedDivisorFamily [IsAffineHom π] : Type u where
453	  /-- The local-equation system on the relative curve. -/
454	  eqns : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations
455	  /-- The finite chart adaptation refining it. -/
456	  adaptation : DivisorAdaptation C R π eqns
457	  /-- The colength certificate of degree `n`. -/
458	  certified : adaptation.IsCertified n

90	## 1. ADJUDICATION A — the dictionary consumption and the off-overlap question (I-0186 item 2 × I-0182)
91	
92	**Question.** Does DD-R consume the one-sided field dictionary {backward map `hsurj` +
93	`divFamDivisor_injective`} with P-fib's divisor normalized off the chart overlap
94	`π⁻¹(Gm)`, or must the general-MV `hdeg` brick be funded?
95	
96	**Verdict: NEITHER. (i) The off-overlap normalization is mathematically unavailable,
97	and (ii) DD-R consumes neither `hsurj` nor `hdeg` — the universal-family architecture
98	replaces the dictionary consumption entirely.** The I-0182 one-sided-dictionary route
99	is hereby SUPERSEDED for DD-R (it remains correct as a statement about the field
100	dictionary; its consumer is DAT-B, see the boundary flag below).
101	
102	**(i) Evidence that off-overlap support cannot be arranged.** P-fib's `D` is the
103	modulus itself, not an auxiliary choice: in `existsUnique_effective_divisor_of_carve`
104	(`PFib.lean:241`) the divisor is *defined* as `D := Scheme.baseDivisor K KM (M•F)`
105	(`PFib.lean:282`) — the base divisor of the *given* window — and the uniqueness clause
106	pins it pointwise by `baseDivisorAt_normalization` (`:127`): the F1 "normalization"
107	normalizes the *window relative to `D`* (no residual base point), never `D`'s support.
108	As the carve point varies over `Z(♦)`, `D` ranges over **every** effective degree-`g`
109	divisor — the ⟸ direction (DD-4 §2.3) embeds `g·x` for every closed `x`, including
110	`x ∈ π⁻¹(Gm)` = the nonempty chart overlap (`relCover`/`pullbackProd`,
111	`RelativeTwoCover.lean:128`; nonemptiness per I-0186). There is no translation (the
112	curve has no group structure) and no rescale (unit rescaling of `K_M` fixes `bd`).
113	I-0186 item 2 is answered: **NO — P-fib's divisor cannot be arranged off-overlap.**
114	
115	**(ii) Why DD-R nevertheless needs no dictionary.** DD-R's backward direction is
116	*pullback of a universal certified family* constructed over `Z(♦)`'s charts by local
117	generators from the universal carve pair (worksheet §3.4.1) — the equations are window
118	*achievers*, never `pointEquations` products; `divFamOfDivisor` appears nowhere. The
119	only degree identity DD-R needs is fibrewise, **for carve-certified families only**,
120	and it closes without Mayer–Vietoris by the **certified-degree pinch** (DDR-2 below):
121	at a field point, `K_M = H⁰(MF − D_F)` (the sections dictionary, DD-4 Task 5's field
122	content) with corank `g` in `H_M`; the section bound
123	(`h0_divisorSheaf_le_max_of_h0_one`, SectionBound:248) forces `deg D_F ≤ 2g` (the F1
124	move, exactly as `PFib.lean:294–303`); then the exact normalization window
125	(`rank_normalization`, WindowLedger:396, licensed at `deg ≤ 2g` by
126	`two_mul_genus_le_M_mul_windowδ`, WindowLedgerF3:102) gives
127	`r_M − g = h⁰(MF − D_F) = Mδ − deg D_F + 1 − g`, i.e. `deg D_F = g`. No adaptation
128	independence, no inclusion–exclusion, no `hdeg`. I-0179's wall is not touched.

131	membership (the pair `ε(F)` satisfies `(♦)`, corank exactly `g`) — never a support

1	/-

3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeFamilySide
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyExtraction
8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.FibrewiseRegular
9	
10	/-!
11	# DDR-3 — the relative local-generator construction (`informal/spec-dd-r.md` §3 item 3)
12	
13	Kleiman `lm:ctn` (ii)⟹(iii)⟹(i) on the relative curve `C_R = relCurve C R` over a
14	Noetherian test ring `R` (the `Z(♦)`-chart rings): from a **theta generator seed** — a
15	choice, at every point `z` of `C_R`, of a pinned chart side, a basic-open neighbourhood
16	piece, and a section of a submodule `K ⊆ H⁰(𝒪(Θᵃ))` whose chart component *generates the
17	subsheaf `K·𝒪` on the piece* (`IsGenerator.dvd`, the Nakayama-neighbourhood clause) and is
18	*fibrewise regular* (`IsGenerator.fibre_regular`, the P-fib input at every `κ(p)`) — this
19	file constructs a `LocalEquations` system with a `DivisorAdaptation` refining it:
20	
21	The flatness ladder and the side-uniform theta components live in
22	`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeFamilySide`; this file assembles them:
23	
24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ThetaGeneratorSeed`, `ThetaGeneratorSeed.IsGenerator` — the seed and
25	  the two `lm:ctn` clauses, stated so that the fibrewise inputs are exactly what P-fib at
26	  `κ(p)` produces (spec §7 risk 2: one named boundary for the DD-4 transport seam);
27	* `ThetaGeneratorSeed.res_eqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors` /
28	  `ThetaGeneratorSeed.germ_eqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors` — **the germ-regularity law**
29	  ((iii)⟹(i)): fibrewise-regular + flat ⟹ regular, through
30	  `Module.Flat.mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_forall_tmul_residueField` on the basic-open
31	  section rings;
32	* `ThetaGeneratorSeed.exists_ratioUnit` — the overlap units: two local generators of the
33	  same subsheaf `K·𝒪` divide each other, and mutual divisibility against a regular
34	  section is a unit ratio;
35	* `ThetaGeneratorSeed.localEquations` / `ThetaGeneratorSeed.divisorAdaptation` — **the
36	  DDR-3 deliverable**: the local-equation system of the seed and a finite chart
37	  adaptation refining it (through the `exists_divisorAdaptation` extraction — no anchor
38	  field of `DivisorAdaptation` is consumed, per the DD-2 carrier-surgery freeze);
39	* `ThetaGeneratorSeed.le_vanishingSubmodule` — **the divisibility law for DDR-4/DDR-5**:
40	  `K ⊆ H⁰(𝒪(Θᵃ − d))` for the constructed system `d` (every element of `K` vanishes
41	  along `d`, germwise).
42	
43	The construction of a seed from the universal carve pair (P-fib achiever choice at each
44	`κ(p)` + `exists_fibrewise_tmul_ne_zero_of_projective`) is the gated follow-up recorded
45	in the DDR-3 lane memory; it consumes `RiemannRoch/DegreeBaseFieldInvariance` and the
46	DD-4 base-field-transport seam and produces exactly a `ThetaGeneratorSeed` with
47	`IsGenerator`.
48	-/
49	
50	set_option autoImplicit false
51	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
52	
53	universe u
54	
55	open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace Opposite
56	open scoped TensorProduct
57	
58	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
59	
60	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
61	
62	
63	/-! ## The theta generator seed and the `lm:ctn` clauses -/
64	
65	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
66	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
67	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π] {a : ℕ}
68	
69	/-- **A theta generator seed for a submodule `K ⊆ H⁰(𝒪(Θᵃ))`** (worksheet §3.4.1): at
70	every point `z` of the relative curve, a pinned chart side containing `z`, a basic-open
71	neighbourhood piece `D(h z)` of the chart, and a global section `sec z ∈ K` — the
72	candidate local generator.  The two `lm:ctn` clauses on a seed are
73	`ThetaGeneratorSeed.IsGenerator`. -/
74	structure ThetaGeneratorSeed (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
75	    [Algebra k R] (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π] (a : ℕ)
76	    (K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)) : Type u where
77	  /-- The pinned chart side of the piece at `z`. -/
78	  side : relCurve C R → Bool
79	  /-- The basic-open generator of the piece at `z`. -/
80	  h : ∀ z : relCurve C R, Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π (side z))
81	  /-- The point lies in its piece. -/
82	  mem_basicOpen : ∀ z : relCurve C R, z ∈ (relCurve C R).basicOpen (h z)
83	  /-- The candidate local generator at `z`. -/
84	  sec : relCurve C R → relThetaSections C R π a
85	  /-- The candidate generators are drawn from `K`. -/
86	  sec_mem : ∀ z, sec z ∈ K
87	
88	namespace ThetaGeneratorSeed
89	
90	variable {K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)} (D : ThetaGeneratorSeed C R π a K)
91	
92	/-- The neighbourhood piece at `z`: the basic open `D(h z)` of the pinned chart. -/
93	noncomputable def piece (z : relCurve C R) : (relCurve C R).Opens :=
94	  (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h z)
95	
96	lemma mem_piece (z : relCurve C R) : z ∈ D.piece z := D.mem_basicOpen z
97	
98	lemma piece_le (z : relCurve C R) : D.piece z ≤ relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z) :=
99	  (relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (D.h z)
100	
101	/-- The pieces are affine (basic opens of the affine pinned charts). -/
102	lemma isAffineOpen_piece (z : relCurve C R) : IsAffineOpen (D.piece z) :=
103	  (isAffineOpen_relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z)).basicOpen (D.h z)
104	
105	/-- **Flatness of the piece sections over the test ring** (the (iii)⟹(i) licence). -/
106	theorem flat_sections_piece (z : relCurve C R) :
107	    Module.Flat R Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z) :=
108	  flat_sections_basicOpen R (isAffineOpen_relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z))
109	    (flat_sections_relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z)) (D.h z)
110	
111	/-- **The candidate local equation at `z`**: the side component of the chosen generator,
112	restricted to the piece. -/
113	noncomputable def eqn (z : relCurve C R) : Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z) :=
114	  relThetaResSide a (D.side z) (D.piece_le z) (D.sec z)
115	
116	/-- **The `lm:ctn` clauses on a seed** (Kleiman (ii)⟹(iii) packaged as its output, plus
117	the fibrewise-regularity input of (iii)⟹(i)):
118	
119	* `dvd` — the chosen generator generates the subsheaf `K·𝒪` on its piece: the side
120	  component of every element of `K` is a multiple of the equation (the Nakayama
121	  neighbourhood clause, produced fibrewise by the P-fib achiever +
122	  `exists_fibrewise_tmul_ne_zero_of_projective`);
123	* `fibre_regular` — the equation is a nonzerodivisor in every residue-field fibre of
124	  every basic sub-open of the piece (produced by P-fib: the fibre of the equation is a
125	  nonzero section of an integral curve over `κ(p)`).
126	
127	Both clauses are stated relative to the test ring only, so the DD-4 base-field-transport
128	seam moves a single boundary (spec-dd-r §7 risk 2). -/
129	structure IsGenerator : Prop where
130	  dvd : ∀ (z : relCurve C R) ⦃ψ : relThetaSections C R π a⦄, ψ ∈ K →
131	    relThetaResSide a (D.side z) (D.piece_le z) ψ ∈ Ideal.span {D.eqn z}
132	  fibre_regular : ∀ (z : relCurve C R) (p : PrimeSpectrum R)
133	      (f : Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z)),
134	    ((relCurve C R).resHom ((relCurve C R).basicOpen_le f) (D.eqn z) ⊗ₜ[R]
135	        (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) ∈
136	      nonZeroDivisors
137	        (Γ(relCurve C R, (relCurve C R).basicOpen f) ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField)
138	
139	variable {D}
140	
141	/-! ### The germ-regularity law ((iii)⟹(i): fibrewise-regular + flat ⟹ regular) -/
142	
143	/-- **Section-level regularity on basic sub-opens of the piece**: the restriction of the
144	equation to any basic open `D(f) ⊆ D(h z)` is a nonzerodivisor — the slicing criterion
145	`Module.Flat.mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_forall_tmul_residueField` over the Noetherian test
146	ring, fed by the seed's fibrewise regularity. -/
147	theorem res_eqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors [IsNoetherianRing R] (hD : D.IsGenerator)
148	    (z : relCurve C R) (f : Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z)) :
149	    (relCurve C R).resHom ((relCurve C R).basicOpen_le f) (D.eqn z)
150	      ∈ nonZeroDivisors Γ(relCurve C R, (relCurve C R).basicOpen f) := by
151	  haveI : Module.Flat R Γ(relCurve C R, (relCurve C R).basicOpen f) :=
152	    flat_sections_basicOpen R (D.isAffineOpen_piece z) (D.flat_sections_piece z) f
153	  exact Module.Flat.mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_forall_tmul_residueField
154	    (fun p => hD.fibre_regular z p f)
155	
156	/-- **The germ-regularity law** ((iii)⟹(i), the `LocalEquations.regular` clause): every
157	germ of the equation on its piece is a nonzerodivisor.  A zerodivisor relation at the
158	stalk descends to a basic sub-open of the piece, where the flat slicing criterion
159	applies. -/
160	theorem germ_eqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors [IsNoetherianRing R] (hD : D.IsGenerator)
161	    (z : relCurve C R) {y : relCurve C R} (hy : y ∈ D.piece z) :
162	    ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.piece z) y hy).hom (D.eqn z)
163	      ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C R).presheaf.stalk y) := by
164	  rw [mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff_right]
165	  intro τ hτ
166	  obtain ⟨V', hyV', t, ht⟩ := (relCurve C R).presheaf.exists_germ_eq τ
167	  -- push the product relation into sections over `V' ⊓ piece z`
168	  have hyW₀ : y ∈ V' ⊓ D.piece z := ⟨hyV', hy⟩

213	/-! ### The overlap ratio units -/
214	
215	/-- **The ratio law of the seed's equations** (the `LocalEquations.ratio_isUnit` clause):
216	on the overlap of two pieces the equations differ by a unit.  Each equation divides the
217	other generator's component (`dvd` crosswise), the side matching transports components
218	across the charts, and mutual divisibility against a regular section is a unit ratio. -/
219	theorem exists_ratioUnit [IsNoetherianRing R] (hD : D.IsGenerator) (z z' : relCurve C R) :
220	    ∃ u : Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z')ˣ,
221	      (relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_left (D.eqn z)
222	        = (u : Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z'))
223	          * (relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_right (D.eqn z') := by
224	  have hWle : D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z'
225	      ≤ relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z) ⊓ relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z') :=
226	    inf_le_inf (D.piece_le z) (D.piece_le z')
227	  -- crosswise divisibility on the pieces
228	  obtain ⟨c₁, hc₁⟩ := Ideal.mem_span_singleton.mp (hD.dvd z (D.sec_mem z'))
229	  obtain ⟨c₂, hc₂⟩ := Ideal.mem_span_singleton.mp (hD.dvd z' (D.sec_mem z))
230	  -- the restricted equations are the side components of the generators on the overlap
231	  have hF1 : (relCurve C R).resHom
232	        (inf_le_left : D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z' ≤ D.piece z) (D.eqn z)
233	      = relThetaResSide a (D.side z) (hWle.trans inf_le_left) (D.sec z) :=
234	    resHom_relThetaResSide a (D.side z) (D.piece_le z) inf_le_left (D.sec z)
235	  have hF2 : (relCurve C R).resHom
236	        (inf_le_right : D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z' ≤ D.piece z') (D.eqn z')
237	      = relThetaResSide a (D.side z') (hWle.trans inf_le_right) (D.sec z') :=
238	    resHom_relThetaResSide a (D.side z') (D.piece_le z') inf_le_right (D.sec z')
239	  -- the crosswise divisibilities, restricted to the overlap
240	  have hF3 : relThetaResSide a (D.side z) (hWle.trans inf_le_left) (D.sec z')
241	      = (relCurve C R).resHom (inf_le_left : D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z' ≤ D.piece z) (D.eqn z)
242	        * (relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_left c₁ := by
243	    have h := congrArg ((relCurve C R).resHom
244	      (inf_le_left : D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z' ≤ D.piece z)) hc₁
245	    rw [map_mul] at h
246	    exact (resHom_relThetaResSide a (D.side z) (D.piece_le z)
247	      inf_le_left (D.sec z')).symm.trans h
248	  have hF4 : relThetaResSide a (D.side z') (hWle.trans inf_le_right) (D.sec z)
249	      = (relCurve C R).resHom
250	          (inf_le_right : D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z' ≤ D.piece z') (D.eqn z')
251	        * (relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_right c₂ := by
252	    have h := congrArg ((relCurve C R).resHom
253	      (inf_le_right : D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z' ≤ D.piece z')) hc₂
254	    rw [map_mul] at h
255	    exact (resHom_relThetaResSide a (D.side z') (D.piece_le z')
256	      inf_le_right (D.sec z)).symm.trans h
257	  -- the side matching for both generators
258	  have hM : ∀ ψ : relThetaSections C R π a,
259	      relThetaResSide a (D.side z) (hWle.trans inf_le_left) ψ
260	        = (relThetaSideUnit a (D.side z) (D.side z') hWle :
261	              Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z'))
262	          * relThetaResSide a (D.side z') (hWle.trans inf_le_right) ψ :=
263	    fun ψ => relThetaResSide_matching a (D.side z) (D.side z') hWle ψ
264	  -- eqn z |_W = (θ · c₂|_W) · eqn z' |_W
265	  have h₁ : (relCurve C R).resHom
266	        (inf_le_left : D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z' ≤ D.piece z) (D.eqn z)
267	      = ((relThetaSideUnit a (D.side z) (D.side z') hWle :
268	            Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z'))
269	          * (relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_right c₂)
270	        * (relCurve C R).resHom
271	            (inf_le_right : D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z' ≤ D.piece z') (D.eqn z') := by
272	    calc (relCurve C R).resHom
273	          (inf_le_left : D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z' ≤ D.piece z) (D.eqn z)
274	        = relThetaResSide a (D.side z) (hWle.trans inf_le_left) (D.sec z) := hF1
275	      _ = (relThetaSideUnit a (D.side z) (D.side z') hWle :
276	            Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z'))
277	          * relThetaResSide a (D.side z') (hWle.trans inf_le_right) (D.sec z) :=
278	        hM (D.sec z)
279	      _ = (relThetaSideUnit a (D.side z) (D.side z') hWle :
280	            Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z'))
281	          * ((relCurve C R).resHom
282	              (inf_le_right : D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z' ≤ D.piece z') (D.eqn z')
283	            * (relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_right c₂) := by rw [hF4]
284	      _ = ((relThetaSideUnit a (D.side z) (D.side z') hWle :
285	            Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z'))
286	          * (relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_right c₂)
287	          * (relCurve C R).resHom
288	              (inf_le_right : D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z' ≤ D.piece z') (D.eqn z') := by
289	        ring
290	  -- eqn z' |_W = (θ⁻¹ · c₁|_W) · eqn z |_W
291	  have hQ : relThetaResSide a (D.side z') (hWle.trans inf_le_right) (D.sec z')
292	      = (((relThetaSideUnit a (D.side z) (D.side z') hWle)⁻¹ :
293	            Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z')ˣ) :
294	            Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z'))
295	        * relThetaResSide a (D.side z) (hWle.trans inf_le_left) (D.sec z') := by
296	    rw [Units.eq_inv_mul_iff_mul_eq]
297	    exact (hM (D.sec z')).symm
298	  have h₂ : (relCurve C R).resHom
299	        (inf_le_right : D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z' ≤ D.piece z') (D.eqn z')
300	      = ((((relThetaSideUnit a (D.side z) (D.side z') hWle)⁻¹ :
301	              Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z')ˣ) :
302	              Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z'))
303	          * (relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_left c₁)
304	        * (relCurve C R).resHom
305	            (inf_le_left : D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z' ≤ D.piece z) (D.eqn z) := by
306	    calc (relCurve C R).resHom
307	          (inf_le_right : D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z' ≤ D.piece z') (D.eqn z')
308	        = relThetaResSide a (D.side z') (hWle.trans inf_le_right) (D.sec z') := hF2
309	      _ = (((relThetaSideUnit a (D.side z) (D.side z') hWle)⁻¹ :
310	              Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z')ˣ) :
311	              Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z'))
312	          * relThetaResSide a (D.side z) (hWle.trans inf_le_left) (D.sec z') := hQ
313	      _ = (((relThetaSideUnit a (D.side z) (D.side z') hWle)⁻¹ :
314	              Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z')ˣ) :
315	              Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z'))
316	          * ((relCurve C R).resHom
317	              (inf_le_left : D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z' ≤ D.piece z) (D.eqn z)
318	            * (relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_left c₁) := by rw [hF3]
319	      _ = ((((relThetaSideUnit a (D.side z) (D.side z') hWle)⁻¹ :
320	              Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z')ˣ) :
321	              Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z'))
322	          * (relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_left c₁)
323	          * (relCurve C R).resHom
324	              (inf_le_left : D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z' ≤ D.piece z) (D.eqn z) := by
325	        ring
326	  -- germwise regularity of the restricted equation
327	  have hreg : ∀ (y : relCurve C R) (hy : y ∈ D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z'),
328	      ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z') y hy).hom
329	        ((relCurve C R).resHom
330	          (inf_le_left : D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z' ≤ D.piece z) (D.eqn z))
331	        ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C R).presheaf.stalk y) := by
332	    intro y hy
333	    rw [show ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z') y hy).hom
334	        ((relCurve C R).resHom
335	          (inf_le_left : D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z' ≤ D.piece z) (D.eqn z))
336	        = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.piece z) y hy.1).hom (D.eqn z) from
337	      TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply _ _ _ _ _]
338	    exact D.germ_eqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors hD z hy.1
339	  exact exists_unit_mul_of_mutual_dvd hreg h₁ h₂

341	/-! ### The DDR-3 deliverable: the local-equation system and its adaptation -/
342	
343	variable (D)
344	
345	/-- **The local-equation system of a theta generator seed** (the DDR-3 family): the
346	pieces are the pointed cover, the equations are the side components of the chosen
347	generators; regularity is the germ-regularity law, the overlap units are the ratio
348	law. -/

350	    (relCurve C R).LocalEquations where
351	  cover := { opens := D.piece, mem_opens := D.mem_piece }
352	  eqn := D.eqn
353	  regular := fun z _ hy => D.germ_eqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors hD z hy
354	  ratio_isUnit := fun z z' => D.exists_ratioUnit hD z z'

362	    (D.localEquations hD).eqn z = D.eqn z := rfl

364	/-- **The finite chart adaptation of the seed's local-equation system**, through the
365	DD-1 extraction (`exists_divisorAdaptation`); no anchor field of `DivisorAdaptation` is
366	consumed here (DD-2 carrier-surgery freeze discipline). -/
367	noncomputable def divisorAdaptation [IsNoetherianRing R] (hD : D.IsGenerator) :
368	    DivisorAdaptation C R π (D.localEquations hD) :=
369	  (exists_divisorAdaptation C R π (D.localEquations hD)).some

375	lemma stalkIdeal_localEquations [IsNoetherianRing R] (hD : D.IsGenerator)

378	      = Ideal.span {((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.piece z) z (D.mem_piece z)).hom

381	/-- **The germ divisibility law**: at any point `y` of the piece of `z`, the germ of the
382	side component of every element of `K` lies in the span of the germ of the equation. -/
383	theorem germ_relThetaResSide_mem_span [IsNoetherianRing R] (hD : D.IsGenerator)

8	/-!
9	# CHART-U(b) — datum-level openness of the chart-membership (witness) locus
10	(`informal/w4-datb-worksheet.md` §1.6, `informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` §3.3)
11	
12	The affine-level heart of the shared CHART-U(b) brick, stated directly on a pinned
13	basic-open cocycle datum in the **witness form** the `chartLocus` predicate uses.
14	
15	For a datum `D` over an affine base `B`, the locus of primes `q` of `B` at which the
16	fibre class of `D` at `κ(q)` admits an effective witness divisor with vanishing `H¹`
17	is Zariski-open in `Spec B`.  This is the single sanctioned openness mechanism of the
18	campaign (`datumRigidEngine_isOpen_vanishing`, Noetherian-free — dat-d §3.5) read
19	through the two-way datum dictionary of C1
20	(`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness`,
21	`informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` GAP-6): the engine open is the complex-form fibre
22	condition `Subsingleton (H¹(pair D) ⊗[B] κ(q))`, and the dictionary rewrites it,
23	pointwise and class-intrinsically, as the effective-witness/h¹-vanishing condition.
24	
25	Role in the CHART-U(b) chain (the two unlanded links of §5 risk 1):
26	
27	* **the shifted-datum constructor (link 1):** over the étale carrier `B` the plus
28	  class collapses to an honest Čech class; twisted by the theta layer and DAT-C's
29	  GAP-1 inverse datum into the `λθᵐ(Σ-shift)⁻¹` class, then extracted
30	  (`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq`) to a datum `D`.  The output of
31	  that link is exactly a `BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π` — the input of the theorem
32	  below, whose witness set is then the `chartLocus`-over-`B`.
33	* **the étale-image openness transport (link 2):** the locus over the test base `A`
34	  is the image, under the (open, surjective) étale carrier map `Spec B → Spec A`, of
35	  the open locus this theorem produces — carried to `A` by mathlib's
36	  `IsOpenMap.isQuotientMap`/`IsQuotientMap.isOpen_preimage` once the fibre-field
37	  invariance identifies the preimage.
38	
39	The theorem is class-intrinsic (any datum in the class has the same witness set, by
40	(V1a)), so a change of extracted representative is free.
41	-/

66	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
67	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

69	/-- **CHART-U(b), the datum-level witness-locus openness** (`w4-datc` §3.3 step (3)):
70	for a pinned basic-open cocycle datum `D` over the affine base `B`, the locus of primes
71	`q` at which the fibre class of `D` at `κ(q)` has an effective witness divisor with
72	vanishing `H¹` is open in `Spec B`.
73	
74	This is `datumRigidEngine_isOpen_vanishing` (the single audited openness engine,
75	Noetherian-free) read in the class/witness form of the `chartLocus` predicate through
76	the two-way datum dictionary
77	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness` (C1, GAP-6):
78	pointwise the engine's complex-form condition `Subsingleton (H¹(pair D) ⊗[B] κ(q))`
79	is exactly the existence of such a witness. -/
80	theorem BasicOpenCocycleDatum.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing
81	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) :
82	    IsOpen {q : PrimeSpectrum B |
83	      ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left).CurveDivisor,
84	        Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass q.asIdeal.ResidueField W
85	            = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B q.asIdeal.ResidueField) D.cechPicClass
86	          ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
87	              ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left.divisorSheaf
88	                q.asIdeal.ResidueField W) 1)} := by
89	  have hset : {q : PrimeSpectrum B |
90	      ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left).CurveDivisor,
91	        Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass q.asIdeal.ResidueField W
92	            = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B q.asIdeal.ResidueField) D.cechPicClass
93	          ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
94	              ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left.divisorSheaf
95	                q.asIdeal.ResidueField W) 1)}
96	      = {p : PrimeSpectrum B |
97	          Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField)} := by
98	    refine Set.ext fun q => ?_
99	    exact (D.subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness q.asIdeal.ResidueField).symm
100	  rw [hset]
101	  exact datumRigidEngine_isOpen_vanishing D hπ
102	
103	/-! ## The openness transport (CHART-U(b) link 2, topological half)
104	
105	The engine produces the open witness locus over the étale carrier `Spec B` (or, on the
106	away pieces, over `Spec (Localization.Away f)`).  CHART-U(b)'s transport (ii)
107	(`w4-datb` §1.6, "the Kleiman tex 2204-2244 step, now one `IsOpenMap` application")
108	carries it down to the test base `Spec A` along the étale carrier map, which is open
109	and surjective.  The pure-topology core of that step is below; the remaining
110	mathematical content of link 2 is the *fibre-field invariance* that identifies the
111	preimage of the base locus with the carrier locus (`κ(q)/κ(p)` a separable extension;
112	`isH1VanishingAt_comap_away_iff` is the landed avatar for the away case). -/
113	
114	/-- **Openness descends along an open continuous surjection**: if `f` is continuous,
115	open, and surjective and `f ⁻¹' V` is open, then `V` is open — because
116	`V = f '' (f ⁻¹' V)` (surjectivity) and `f` carries opens to opens.  This is the
117	topological core of CHART-U(b)'s transport (ii). -/
118	theorem isOpen_of_isOpen_preimage_of_isOpenMap_surjective
119	    {X Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] {f : X → Y}
120	    (hcont : Continuous f) (hopen : IsOpenMap f) (hsurj : Function.Surjective f)
121	    {V : Set Y} (hV : IsOpen (f ⁻¹' V)) : IsOpen V :=
122	  ((hopen.isQuotientMap hcont hsurj).isOpen_preimage).mp hV
123	
124	/-- **The `Spec`-level openness transport of CHART-U(b)** (transport (ii), topological
125	half): for a ring map `f : R →+* S` whose induced `Spec S → Spec R` is open and
126	surjective (e.g. an étale carrier map), a locus of `Spec R` whose preimage in `Spec S`
127	is open is itself open.  The engine's open witness locus lives on the carrier `Spec S`;
128	this pushes it to the test base `Spec R`. -/
129	theorem isOpen_of_isOpen_comap_preimage {R S : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
130	    (f : R →+* S) (hopen : IsOpenMap (PrimeSpectrum.comap f))
131	    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap f))
132	    {V : Set (PrimeSpectrum R)} (hV : IsOpen (PrimeSpectrum.comap f ⁻¹' V)) :
133	    IsOpen V :=
134	  isOpen_of_isOpen_preimage_of_isOpenMap_surjective
135	    (PrimeSpectrum.continuous_comap f) hopen hsurj hV
136	
137	end AlgebraicGeometry
